divergences.reference_behavior: Only the compatible provider validates the response envelope; TypeSafe, OpenRouter, and Cloudflare coerce a missing answers object to {} and each tool then reports per-item invalid_response (quirk Q1).
divergences.python_behavior: Every provider applies the compatible envelope rules and raises one provider error, so a broken envelope is a transport failure, not a set of judgments.

divergences.reference_behavior: A truncation cut that splits a surrogate pair keeps the lone high surrogate (quirk Q8).
divergences.python_behavior: The split pair is dropped whole, so the truncated result is one UTF-16 unit shorter.

divergences.reference_behavior: Auto resolution reaches Jev on the Vercel AI Gateway through experimental_evaluate().
divergences.python_behavior: The Vercel slot keeps its resolution order position but raises a clear unsupported-provider error instead of emulating it.

divergences.reference_behavior: Redacts only JEV_API_KEY, and only on the compatible provider's error body (quirk Q9).
divergences.python_behavior: Every configured secret is redacted on every provider, on every error path and log line, with URL-userinfo variants covered.

divergences.reference_behavior: A cancelled MCP call keeps its Jev request running to completion (quirk Q10).
divergences.python_behavior: Cancellation aborts the in-flight request and kills only this call's regex worker; nothing cancelled writes to stdout afterwards.

divergences.reference_behavior: Any pattern V8's RegExp accepts runs, in UTF-16 unit space; catastrophic patterns end in the timeout text.
divergences.python_behavior: stdlib re matches a narrower translated subset; patterns outside it get invalid_pattern with a named reason, and re stalling like V8 keeps the timeout fixtures honest.

divergences.reference_behavior: No cross-call pool exists; the reference runs one worker thread per call, so queueing never affects output.
divergences.python_behavior: One absolute deadline spans admission, worker start, IPC, and matching; under saturation a pattern the reference would have executed can fail without running.

divergences.reference_behavior: Not applicable: the reference has no cross-call pool and no saturation path.
divergences.python_behavior: A pattern refused at the queue bound reports the stable reason token regex_pool_saturated instead of the regex-timeout text, so capacity pressure is not misread as a pattern problem.

divergences.reference_behavior: No provider request carries a timeout anywhere in askJev; a provider that stops answering keeps the tool call waiting until the client cancels.
divergences.python_behavior: Runtime.ask still passes no whole-call deadline (the client's MCP cancellation is the recovery path for the call), but every provider attempt is bounded by the retry policy's 30 s per-attempt deadline and the whole bounded sequence by its 90 s budget, so a hung connection becomes a bounded, retryable failure and a transient one is retried (ADR-0057).

divergences.reference_behavior: The reference is stdio-only; no HTTP transport exists to compare against.
divergences.python_behavior: streamable-http is an experimental Tier B extension for 1.0: localhost by default, no reliability contract of its own (provider attempts are bounded per ADR-0057, but there is no admission control and no load-tested limits), promotion requires P9 evidence. A bind outside 127.0.0.1/localhost/::1 additionally requires a bearer token (http-bearer-token-required).

divergences.reference_behavior: The reference is stdio-only; no HTTP transport exists to compare against.
divergences.python_behavior: streamable-http refuses to start without JEV_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN on any host the SDK does not protect (exactly 127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1 get Host/Origin validation; every other host, including other loopback spellings, requires the token); with a token set, every request must carry Authorization: Bearer or get 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer before any MCP handling.

divergences.reference_behavior: Node fetch follows redirects; a cross-origin 307/308 re-sends the request body, carrying the caller's state to the redirect target.
divergences.python_behavior: HttpProvider rejects a redirect that changes origin before the next request is sent; same-origin redirects keep httpx's own method semantics.

divergences.reference_behavior: Node fetch follows redirects, including cross-origin, with the request body.
divergences.python_behavior: The typesafe-sdk transport rides the SDK's own httpx2 client; its redirect policy is not guarded at our layer and is unaudited (ADR-0023 scope note).

divergences.reference_behavior: Unknown: the reference's initialize response was never captured.
divergences.python_behavior: mcp 2.2 advertises prompts, resources, and experimental alongside tools; the Python shape is pinned, the comparison against the reference is pending a capture.

divergences.reference_behavior: No signal handler: the Node process dies by signal with a signal exit code.
divergences.python_behavior: SIGINT and SIGTERM stop the loop and exit 0 without a traceback, stdio and HTTP alike.

divergences.reference_behavior: The reference accepts a JSON-RPC frame containing a lone surrogate escape and echoes it back as the same escape.
divergences.python_behavior: Streamable HTTP keeps the MCP SDK's parser, which refuses the frame with a -32700 reply (id null) before any tool runs. stdio serves it as the reference does (src/jev_judge_mcp/stdio.py).

divergences.reference_behavior: The reference sends HTTP-Referer naming its own repository on every OpenRouter request.
divergences.python_behavior: This server sends HTTP-Referer naming this repository (https://github.com/PyModel/jev-judge-mcp) on every OpenRouter request; nothing else about the request changes.

divergences.reference_behavior: An omitted classify id becomes {kind}{index} with no check against supplied ids, so a later entry with that id overwrites the earlier one and both rows report the same id at auto (quirk Q11).
divergences.python_behavior: A generated id that equals an id already used for that items or classes list raises Duplicate {kind} id before any provider request.

divergences.reference_behavior: The Node reference starts on any operating system through npx, including Windows.
divergences.python_behavior: On a non-POSIX platform (sys.platform starting with win) the process exits at startup with one message naming that platform, before signal handlers or the extract worker pool.

divergences.reference_behavior: Only environment variables provide credentials; a missing TYPESAFE_API_KEY fails resolution with the frozen no-credentials text.
divergences.python_behavior: A key stored by `jev-judge-mcp setup` (0600 file, live-verified before storing) fills the typesafe slot when the variable is unset; the variable always wins, blank or missing files behave exactly as before, and the stored value joins the redaction set when read.

divergences.reference_behavior: Every tool call sends a provider request; nothing is replayed from disk.
divergences.python_behavior: With JEV_MCP_CACHE on (off by default), a byte-identical request — provider, model, state, questions — replays the recorded Evaluation verbatim from the cache directory; tool payloads stay byte-identical to the first answer's, and a corrupt or foreign record is a miss.

divergences.reference_behavior: The reference publishes exactly ten tools; no tool exposes a caller-supplied score rubric.
divergences.python_behavior: jev_score is published after the snapshot ten (the snapshot stays a byte-identical prefix of tools/list): one score question over a caller rubric of 2-10 levels, strict whole-answer validation (validate_rubric_answer), ADR-owned caps in limits.SCORE, and no policy thresholds.

divergences.reference_behavior: jev_compare judges the overall independently of the aspects: an aspect that reports contradicts under a same_fact or different_facts overall changes nothing in the output.
divergences.python_behavior: The overall is unchanged, but a non-empty warnings field names the contradicting aspects in jev_decide's warning style; the field is absent when no aspect contradicts, so every unaffected output stays byte-identical to the reference.

divergences.reference_behavior: initialize reports serverInfo.version as the reference package version (0.5.0), with no local suffix.
divergences.python_behavior: A wheel, and a git checkout whose HEAD commit is exactly the tag v<version>, report the installed version. Any other git source tree of this distribution reports the PEP 440 local version <version>+g<short sha>. serverInfo.name stays jev-mcp.

divergences.reference_behavior: Gate, verify, review, and find return the reference payload. Claim questions tell the model not to use diff and tests. Verify questions have no anti-injection sentence. A sanitized or de-duplicated id is not mapped back to the id the caller sent.
divergences.python_behavior: Additive fields are appended. Gate sends diff and tests as implicit evidence and drops the ignore-them sentence. Verify questions gain the role sentence and the anti-injection sentence. Find, verify, and gate append renamed_ids (sent id -> returned id) when id sanitization or de-duplication changed a caller id. Old keys stay. See also ADR-0063, ADR-0067, and ADR-0068.

divergences.reference_behavior: The reference initialize response was never captured, and this server previously sent no instructions.
divergences.python_behavior: initialize.instructions names each published tool once and says when to call jev_gate and to honor action. No threshold numbers, secrets, or harness names.

divergences.reference_behavior: diff is a string. Evidence items are id and text only. tests is a string.
divergences.python_behavior: jev_gate and jev_review also accept a file list. Evidence items may carry kind and role. tests_format and tests_sha256 are optional. ADR-0067.

divergences.reference_behavior: Array-typed arguments are described by what they are for; the item shape is only implied by the items schema.
divergences.python_behavior: The description of every array-typed argument states its item shape plainly: claims, requirements, aspects, and rubric levels are plain strings; evidence items, classify items and classes, decide and find/rerank candidates, extract fields, and review/gate file lists are objects with named keys. A caller that pattern-matches from another jev surface cannot mis-shape its first call. No constraint changes: the items schemas are untouched and jev_screen stays byte-identical (ADR-0013 amendment, 2026-09-25).

divergences.reference_behavior: An isError result has one content text block, the error text. There is no second block and no structuredContent, so a client that reads only content does not see a typed code.
divergences.python_behavior: content[0].text stays byte-equal to that error text. A second content text block is the compact JSON object {"code": "<code>"}. structuredContent.code stays. Success results stay one block.
